families.familyTitle: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties

claims.statement: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension.
assumptions: The abelian variety is complex.
The abelian variety has complex multiplication.
claims.conclusion: Every rational Hodge class on such a variety is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes.

families.familyTitle: The geometric case of the Erdős similarity conjecture

claims.statement: For every fixed $`q\in(0,1)`$, constructs compact subsets of $`[0,1]`$ with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of $`\{q^n:n\ge1\}`$, with dilations of either sign.
assumptions: q is a fixed real number in (0,1).
Translations are arbitrary real numbers.
Dilations are nonzero real numbers of either sign.
claims.conclusion: For every eta in (0,1), there is a compact set E_{q,eta} contained in [0,1] of measure greater than 1-eta that contains no nontrivial affine copy of {q^n : n >= 1}, for any translation and either sign of nonzero dilation.

leanDeclaration.statement: For every $0<\eta<1$, it constructs a compact set $E\subset[0,1]$ of measure greater than $1-\eta$ that contains no affine copy of $\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}$.

coverage.scopeExcerpt: The formalization proves the dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture. For every $0<\eta<1$, it constructs a compact set $E\subset[0,1]$ of measure greater than $1-\eta$ that contains no affine copy of $\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}$.

claims.statement: We construct a compact subset of the unit interval, of measure arbitrarily close to one, that contains no affine copy of the dyadic sequence $`\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}`$. The conclusion holds for every translation and every nonzero real dilation, of either sign, proving the dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture.
assumptions: The sequence is the dyadic sequence {2^{-n} : n >= 1}.
Translations are arbitrary real numbers.
Dilations are nonzero real numbers of either sign.
claims.conclusion: There is a compact set E contained in [0,1] with measure arbitrarily close to one that contains no affine copy of {2^{-n} : n >= 1}.

leanDeclaration.statement: For every $0<\eta<1$, it constructs a compact set $E\subset[0,1]$ of measure greater than $1-\eta$ that contains no affine copy of $\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}$.

coverage.scopeExcerpt: The formalization proves the dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture. families.familyTitle: Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds

claims.statement: Proves Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length.
assumptions: The set consists of positive integers.
The sum of reciprocals over the set diverges.
claims.conclusion: For every requested finite length, the set contains an arithmetic progression with positive common difference.

claims.statement: Quantitatively, for each fixed k ≥ 3, every subset of $`\{1,\ldots,N\}`$ with no nonconstant k-term progression has size at most $`C_kN\exp[-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}]`$, with positive constants depending only on k.
assumptions: k >= 3 is a fixed integer.
The subset of {1,...,N} contains no nonconstant k-term arithmetic progression.
C_k, c_k, and epsilon_k are positive constants depending only on k.
claims.conclusion: r_k(N) <= C_k N exp(-c_k (log N)^{epsilon_k}), where r_k(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1,...,N} with no nonconstant k-term arithmetic progression.

claims.statement: Proves that the edges of every finite simple undirected graph on n vertices can be partitioned into at most $`Cn`$ simple cycles and single edges, for an absolute constant C. This resolves the Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture, bounding the number of pieces linearly even for dense graphs.
assumptions: The graph is finite, simple, and undirected.
The graph has n vertices.
C is an absolute positive constant independent of n.
claims.conclusion: The edge set has an edge-disjoint partition into at most Cn simple cycles and single edges; edgeless and small graphs are included.

leanDeclaration.statement: every finite simple graph on $n$ vertices has an edge-disjoint decomposition into at most $Cn$ cycles or singleton edges

coverage.scopeExcerpt: The Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture asks for a linear bound on the number of cycles and single edges needed to partition a graph's edges. The formalized result gives one absolute constant $C>0$ such that every finite simple graph on $n$ vertices has an edge-disjoint decomposition into at most $Cn$ cycles or singleton edges. Edgeless and small graphs are included. The optimal value of $C$ is not determined.
coverage.note: The upstream scope document states the linear bound with an absolute constant C and notes that the optimal value of C is not determined.
